analysis: Brown adipose tissue is primarily involved in thermogenesis, which is the production of heat, especially in response to cold. This is a well-established function of brown adipose tissue. Unilocular adipocytes, found in white adipose tissue, contain a single large lipid droplet that is not delimited by a membrane but is surrounded by the cytoplasm. Leptin, secreted by adipocytes, actually suppresses appetite rather than stimulating intake. White adipose tissue is well-vascularized to facilitate the storage and mobilization of lipids.
